claim: "the attorney's name and ID (021041994) appear on New Jersey's administrative ineligibility lists in 2024, 2025 and the current list to 9 November 2026"
problem: The 2024 element has no source URL anywhere in the audit's Sources list (only the 2026 Client Protection Fund list and the 2025 IOLTA list are cited). The statement is true - I found 'HUGHES MARK FABIAN III 021041994' on the 2024 IOLTA ineligible list at https://www.njcourts.gov/sites/default/files/notices/2024/09/n240910a.pdf - but as delivered it is not traceable to a cited page. Note also that the same name/ID appears on the 2018 IOLTA list (https://www.njcourts.gov/sites/default/files/notices/2018/10/n181023e.pdf), so '2024, 2025' understates a longer pattern.
fix: Add the 2024 IOLTA list URL to Sources and, optionally, phrase it as 'listed on NJ administrative ineligibility lists repeatedly since 2018, including 2024, 2025 and the list running to 9 November 2026'.

claim: https://www.njcourts.gov/host/attyapps/GoodStandingStatusDefinitions.pdf is cited for 'a listed attorney cannot currently practice'
problem: The cited URL returns HTTP 404. I could not open it. The claim itself is correct and still verifiable, in the current NJ Courts document 'Definitions and Explanations for Attorney Status' (library.njcourts.gov): administrative ineligibility 'is not the result of discipline, but attorneys who are administratively ineligible are not allowed to practice New Jersey law.'

claim: Intake has "no hours, no voicemail-to-email, no form and no scheduler"
problem: 'No voicemail-to-email' is a claim about the firm's telephone system, which no public source can establish; I could not verify it (the site, Lawyers.com and Martindale show nothing about voicemail). As written it may be wrong and would undercut credibility if the attorney has voicemail forwarding.
fix: Limit it to what is observable: 'no published hours, no form, no booking and no after-hours option on the site'.

claim: Document title: "Law Office of Mark F. Hughes III"
problem: No source I opened uses this firm name. The site brands him 'MARK F HUGHES III Attorney-at-Law'; Martindale says 'Member at Mark F. Hughes III, Esquire'; Lawyers.com lists the firm as 'Mark F. Hughes III, Esquire'.
fix: Use the name the directories use ('Mark F. Hughes III, Esquire') or note it as the practice of Mark F. Hughes III.

claim: Founder email: "a deadline register covering the state filings that show up on the ineligibility lists"
problem: Tone risk rather than a factual error: the sentence gestures at his ineligibility without naming it, which can read as a veiled hint to a lawyer who knows exactly what those lists mean.
fix: Say it plainly and neutrally, e.g. 'the annual filings (assessment, IOLTA, CLE) that, if missed, put an attorney on the state's ineligible lists - a register keeps them on schedule'.
